item.title: Version 2.0
item.description:
Ankylix 2.0 is a free update for everyone who bought 1.x.

  • Peek. In the window switcher, press ⇧ and a window's letter (or hold the letter) to bring it to the front for a quick look — framed in orange, ready to scroll or copy from. Tab moves to the next window; Esc puts everything back where it was. ⌃⌥P peeks at the last window again.
  • App groups. ⌃⌥⇧G saves the apps on screen, and where their windows are, under a name. ⌃⌥G and a letter bring a group back: closed apps launch, every window returns to its place and the apps outside the group are hidden.
  • Open here. In layout mode, ⇧ and a zone's letter places the window and makes that zone where its app opens from now on. In move & resize, P does the same with the window's exact frame. Manage both in the new Preferences → Apps.
  • Key hints in every mode. Pause in a mode and a panel lists its keys, placed where it covers nothing. Choose when and where it appears in Preferences → General.
  • Never forget a trigger. Hold ⌃⌥ for a moment to see every trigger; the menu bar menu lists them too. Ankylix also suggests the shortcut when you move or switch windows with the mouse.
  • Digits now switch layouts without moving anything. Press Return to apply the layout on screen.
  • Press the layouts trigger in move & resize to go straight to layouts.
  • The switcher opens the minimized-windows list straight away when no window is on screen.
  • Shortcuts keep working while Preferences is open.
  • Ankylix asks for Input Monitoring only when macOS needs it, offers to reset a stale entry, and shows its status in Preferences.
  • Fixed: move & resize keys could stop working after switching windows, and the window picked in the switcher could fall behind.

item.title: Version 1.4
item.description:
• Apply a whole layout with one key. In layout mode, press a digit and every zone fills — the focused window takes the first zone, your most recent windows the rest. Press Return to apply the layout on screen. A letter still places the focused window, and swaps it with whatever is in that zone.
  • The last layout you used is remembered across launches.
  • Stable hints in the window switcher. Each app's window gets the app's initial (S = Safari, X = Xcode), so after a few jumps you stop reading. The minimized-windows panel key moved from M to , so M can be a hint.
  • New default shortcuts: ⌃⌥L (layouts), ⌃⌥W (switcher), ⌃⌥M (move/resize). The old ⌘⇧O and ⌘⇧F were Open Quickly / Find in Files in every major editor. If you never changed the defaults, Ankylix moves you over and tells you.
  • Ankylix now warns when a shortcut clashes with a menu command in the app you're using, or is already taken by another app. Preferences → Shortcuts shows clashes while you choose.
  • One permission instead of two. Input Monitoring is no longer requested — Accessibility covers it — and the forced relaunch after setup is gone.
  • A welcome step after setup shows the shortcuts to try.
  • Layout mode now ends on a click or an app switch instead of swallowing keys until Esc.
  • Fixed: the Permissions panel could stay red after a permission was granted.

item.title: Version 1.2
item.description:
• One-click activation. After buying, the purchase page now has an Activate Ankylix button that opens the app and activates it for you — no more copying a Transaction ID out of your receipt.
  • Fixed: activation links opened from the website were ignored while the permission setup prompts were on screen.
  • Fixed: the purchase button showed the price in dollars; Ankylix is €19.
  • The 14-day trial now ends properly. Previously the app kept working after the trial expired; now it stops until you activate a license.
